source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which characteristic describes a benign tumor?
questions.rationale: Benign tumors are encapsulated, well differentiated, slow-growing, and do not metastasize.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Characteristics of Tumor (PDF p. 284)
questions.quote: Encapsulation (+) (-)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A malignant tumor of bone tissue is called:
questions.rationale: '-oma' usually denotes benign tumors; sarcomas arise from connective tissue such as bone.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tumor Nomenclature (PDF p. 284)
questions.quote: Osteosarcoma

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In TNM staging, the 'N' refers to:
questions.rationale: TNM: Tumor extent, Node involvement, Metastasis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Grading vs Staging (PDF p. 285)
questions.quote: Node: lymph node involvement

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Classifying tumor cells by how much they resemble the tissue of origin is called:
questions.rationale: Grading classifies cells by differentiation; staging determines size, invasion, and metastasis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Grading vs Staging (PDF p. 285)
questions.quote: Refers to the classification of tumor cells

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In carcinogenesis, altered cells invade adjacent tissue and metastasize during:
questions.rationale: Initiation alters DNA, promotion expresses mutant genes, progression invades and metastasizes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Carcinogenesis (PDF p. 285)
questions.quote: Invade adjacent tissues and metastasize

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is a cancer warning sign the nurse should teach?
options: A sore that does not heal
questions.rationale: CAUTION US signs include a sore that does not heal, unusual bleeding, and a nagging cough.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Warning Signs (PDF p. 285)
questions.quote: A sore that does not heal

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which test confirms a cancer diagnosis?
questions.rationale: Biopsy obtains tissue for cell analysis and is definitive; imaging and markers support diagnosis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Diagnostic Tests (PDF p. 286)
questions.quote: Obtaining tissue sample for analysis of cells.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Freezing tumor tissue with liquid nitrogen is called:
questions.rationale: Cryosurgery uses liquid nitrogen to freeze and destroy tissue.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Surgery (PDF p. 286)
questions.quote: Cryosurgery: liquid nitrogen is used to freeze tissue

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client receiving external beam radiation asks about skin care. The nurse advises:
options: Do not wash off the skin markings
questions.rationale: Keep markings, avoid ointments, lotions, and powders, and protect skin from heat.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, External Radiation (PDF p. 286)
questions.quote: Do not remove the markings on the area.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A visitor asks whether a client on external beam radiation is radioactive. The nurse answers:
options: No, the client emits no radiation
questions.rationale: In teletherapy the source is outside the body; the client is not radioactive.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, External Radiation (PDF p. 286)
questions.quote: Client is NOT radioactive (does not emit radiation).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which nurse should not be assigned to a client with a cervical radium implant?
questions.rationale: Never assign pregnant staff, and do not allow child visitors, for brachytherapy clients.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Brachytherapy (PDF p. 287)
questions.quote: Never assign a pregnant hospital staff to the client.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which radiation safety principle protects the nurse caring for a client with an implant?
questions.rationale: Limit time, keep distance (about 6 feet), and use shielding with a dosimeter badge.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Brachytherapy (PDF p. 287)
questions.quote: Distance: Maintain six (6) feet away from client.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During intracavitary brachytherapy for cervical cancer, which diet is ordered?
questions.rationale: Low-residue diet slows bowel movement to prevent dislodging the implant; bed rest and catheter are used.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Brachytherapy (PDF p. 287)
questions.quote: Low-residue/Low-fiber diet: to slow down bowel movement and prevent defecation.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client received oral iodine-131 for thyroid cancer. Which instruction is correct?
questions.rationale: With unsealed sources, body fluids are radioactive: flush 3 times and do not share the toilet.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Unsealed Brachytherapy (PDF p. 287)
questions.quote: Flush the toilet 3 times after voiding/defecating.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Vincristine acts on the cell cycle by:
questions.rationale: Mitotic inhibitors (vincristine, vinblastine, paclitaxel) arrest metaphase.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mitotic Inhibitors (PDF p. 288)
questions.quote: Arrest metaphase by inhibiting mitotic tubular formation

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which chemotherapy drug is an antimetabolite?
questions.rationale: Antimetabolites (methotrexate, 6-MP, cytarabine) block enzymes needed for DNA synthesis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-metabolites (PDF p. 287)
questions.quote: Methotrexate

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which antineoplastic class crosses the blood-brain barrier, useful for brain tumors?
questions.rationale: Nitrosoureas (carmustine, lomustine) cross the blood-brain barrier.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nitrosoureas (PDF p. 288)
questions.quote: Cross the blood-brain barrier

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Trastuzumab and rituximab belong to which class?
questions.rationale: Monoclonal antibodies target cancer cells while sparing normal cells.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Monoclonal Antibodies (PDF p. 289)
questions.quote: Destroy cancer cells and spare normal cells

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which practice is correct when preparing chemotherapy drugs?
options: Wear gloves, gown, and face shield
Prepare in a closed small room
questions.rationale: Use full PPE, a well-ventilated area, hazard labels, and leak- and puncture-proof disposal.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Preparing Chemo Drugs (PDF p. 289)
questions.quote: Wear gloves at all times.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A chemotherapy drug spills on the counter. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Spills are cleaned with a designated spill kit.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Handling Waste (PDF p. 289)
questions.quote: In case of spillage of chemotherapeutic drugs, use a spill kit for clean-up.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How should antiemetics be scheduled for a client on highly emetogenic chemotherapy?
questions.rationale: Give antiemetics round-the-clock; nausea may last 24–48 hours and recur up to a week later.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nausea & Vomiting (PDF p. 289)
questions.quote: Round-the-clock medications.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When does chemotherapy-induced alopecia usually begin?
questions.rationale: Hair loss begins 2–3 weeks after starting; regrowth may begin around 8 weeks after therapy.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Alopecia (PDF p. 289)
questions.quote: Begins 2 to 3 weeks

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which mouth care is appropriate for chemotherapy-induced stomatitis?
questions.rationale: Use saline rinses, a soft brush, and a bland diet; avoid alcohol mouthwash, spicy, and citrus foods.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stomatitis (PDF p. 290)
questions.quote: Saline mouth rinse. Never use alcohol-based commercial mouthwash.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why is viscous lidocaine avoided for stomatitis in children?
questions.rationale: Viscous lidocaine can suppress the gag reflex, increasing aspiration risk in children.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Stomatitis (PDF p. 290)
questions.quote: Contraindicated: Child (suppressed gag reflex)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A neutropenic client's relative brings fresh flowers. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Neutropenic precautions exclude fresh flowers and raw foods to reduce infection risk.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Neutropenia (PDF p. 290)
questions.quote: Neutropenic diet: No flowers, fresh fruits, vegetables, raw food.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia needs to shave. The nurse provides:
questions.rationale: Bleeding precautions: electric razor, soft toothbrush, no enemas, suppositories, or antiplatelets.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Thrombocytopenia (PDF p. 290)
questions.quote: No shaving using straight razors. Use electric razor.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which order should the nurse question for a client with a platelet count of 20,000/mm³?
questions.rationale: Avoid suppositories and enemas because of bleeding risk; use stool softeners.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Thrombocytopenia (PDF p. 290)
questions.quote: No suppositories and enema. Use stool softeners.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which drug is given for chemotherapy-induced anemia?
questions.rationale: Erythropoietin stimulates RBC production; schedule rest periods with activities.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anemia (PDF p. 290)
questions.quote: Administer erythropoietin as ordered.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Clay-colored stools and rapid weight loss in a 70-year-old smoker suggest cancer of the:
questions.rationale: Pancreatic cancer causes abdominal pain, weight loss, glucose problems, and acholic stools from biliary obstruction.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pancreatic Cancer (PDF p. 291)
questions.quote: Clay-colored stools (Acholic stools)
